title: Everton Blair wins Georgia 13th District special election runoff
dek: Everton Blair Jr., former chair of the Gwinnett County School Board, defeated Marcye Scott in Tuesday's special election runoff for Georgia's 13th Congressional District. Blair will serve the remainder of Rep. David Scott's term, which ends in January. The seat will be contested again in November between Democratic state Rep. Jasmine Clark and Republican Jonathan Chavez.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: Blair won the runoff to serve the remaining few months of David Scott's final term in a district that has consistently favored Democratic candidates by large margins.
bottom_line: Blair holds the seat for a few months before the November general election between Clark and Chavez reshapes the district's representation. Watch for early 2027 when Clark or Chavez begins the full two-year term.
body: Everton Blair Jr., former chair of the Gwinnett County School Board, defeated Marcye Scott in Tuesday's special election runoff for Georgia's 13th Congressional District, per CBS News. Blair will serve the remaining few months of Rep. David Scott's term, which ends in January.

Blair advanced to the runoff after finishing second out of five candidates in the July 28 nonpartisan special election, according to CBS News. The runoff pitted him against Scott's daughter, Marcye Scott, who had finished first in July.

Rep. David Scott, who held the seat, died in April. The 13th District has been extremely favorable for Democratic candidates. Scott won his 2024 re-election bid with about 72% of the vote, and then-Vice President Kamala Harris received about 71% of the vote in the district, per CBS News.

Blair placed third in the May 19 Democratic primary for the full two-year term that will be decided in November, according to CBS News. In that race, Democratic state Rep. Jasmine Clark and Republican Jonathan Chavez will face each other for the seat beginning in January, per CBS News. Clark advanced from the Democratic primary as the top vote-getter.
The Associated Press projects Blair will complete the remainder of Scott's final term.
